question: Positive finite float measured rates admitted by planner may fail strict integer-only artifact parsing.

sources.finding: parse_float controls decoding of JSON non-integer tokens; parse_constant separately controls NaN/Infinity tokens. Default encoder permits nonfinite values unless allow_nan=False.
Planner accepts type int or float, finite and positive; MigrationPlan calls decode_manifest_json.
parse_float and parse_constant both use integer-only rejection.

constraints: Do not broaden numeric admission in manifests, compiler locks, generations or IDs.
Keep finite positive measured-rate semantics and canonical artifact bytes explicit.
Reproduce public planner path on authorized PostgreSQL before choosing correction.
alternatives: Explicit artifact-only whitelist for finite positive rate paths, leaving manifest parser strict.
Versioned decimal-string or rational rate representation; requires compatibility work.
Reject float API inputs explicitly; does not satisfy the currently implied finite-float support and leaves objective open.
real_pg_red: Both public planner paths fail at finite20.5/10.25 rates:2FAIL0.70s
chosen_design: Separate bounded transition-artifact decoder; only two rate paths plus reverse source-plan rate paths admit positive finite floats. Shared manifest decoder remains untouched.
alternatives_decision: Versioned decimal/rational representation adds schema/reader complexity; rounding would alter input estimates. Field-scoped decoding preserves JSON float semantics already accepted at the planner API while keeping other numeric paths strict.
compatibility: Prior integer-only artifacts remain byte-identical. New fractional-rate artifacts require the corrected reader; older readers refuse them.
